title: Email
description: Transactional email: a Mailer service on Cloudflare Email Service, printed to the console in development, a dashboard card, plus invitation emails with organizations.

envVars.name: MAIL_FROM
envVars.description: Sender address; its domain must be enabled for Cloudflare Email Sending (wrangler email sending enable <domain>)

envVars.name: MAIL_TRANSPORT
envVars.description: cloudflare (default) sends through the EMAIL binding; console prints emails instead (used by .dev.vars)

args.name: mailTransport

args.content:
## Email

- Send mail through the `Mailer` service from `@repo/core` (`send({ to, subject, text, html? })`); do not use the `EMAIL` binding directly. Always send a `text` body. `sendTestEmail` in `packages/core/src/mailer.ts` is a program that uses it.
- `MailerLive` in `apps/web/src/server/mailer.ts` picks the transport from `MAIL_TRANSPORT`: `console` (set for local development) prints the message to the dev server log, anything else sends through Cloudflare Email Service with the `EMAIL` `send_email` binding. `MAIL_FROM` must be an address on a domain enabled for sending: `wrangler email sending enable <domain>`. The dashboard card's server functions are in `apps/web/src/server/email-demo.ts`.
- Test with `MailerInMemory` from `packages/core/test/mailer-in-memory.ts`, which records messages in `SentMail` instead of sending them, as `mailer.test.ts` does.
- Transactional mail only (invitations, receipts, password resets); use a dedicated platform for marketing or bulk sends.
- On auth stacks efforge chains `.middleware([requireSession])` on the card's server functions in `email-demo.ts`; gate any server function you add that sends mail the same way.

### Email without auth

- While this project has no auth, the test email server function in `apps/web/src/server/email-demo.ts` is open: with `MAIL_TRANSPORT=cloudflare`, anyone who can reach the app can send mail from your domain. Add auth (`efforge add auth/better-auth`, which guards it) or remove the demo before deploying.

### Invitation emails

- `organization({ sendInvitationEmail })` in `auth.ts` calls `invitation-email.ts`, which emails the `/accept-invite/<id>` link through the `Mailer`. A failed send is logged and does not fail the invitation; the link is still shown to the inviter.
